author.name: Data Dave
author.role: Builds secure, scalable data pipelines and manages storage infrastructure. Focuses on high-quality data operations and robust data governance. Collaborates on exploring data and managing data quality to support model development.

challenge.name: The Midnight Deadline
challenge.description: The nightly data job is failing to finish before the store managers open the ordering app. #reliability_ruth# demands an automated validation layer to catch bad data instantly so the morning window is never missed again. #data_dave# insists on keeping the process manual for now, arguing that the infrastructure costs are too high and the current manual checks are sufficient to manage the risk.

output.content: I am willing to accept the cost of an automated validation layer if it removes the manual effort I currently spend on nightly checks. The infrastructure expense is high, but I would give up the time I burn on hand checking the till feeds to get the reliability {reliability_ruth.first} is asking for. As long as the manual process is my only tool, I am defending it because the alternative is unaffordable. But if automation cuts that labor, I am not opposed to moving forward. I am trading my current manual workload for the capital outlay, provided the system actually catches the bad data before the morning window opens.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states they are willing to give up the time spent on manual nightly checks in exchange for accepting the high infrastructure costs of an automated validation layer.
